topic: Why American men live about 5 years less than women (CDC 2024 gap 4.9, 1900 about 2, 1980 nearly 8)

voice.note: one file per block or one merged file; never change the words

blocks.voice_text: American men live about five years less than women. And it wasn't always five.
blocks.screen_text: American men live about 5 years less than women. And it wasn't always 5.

blocks.voice_text: In nineteen hundred, the gap was only two years. By nineteen eighty, it was nearly eight. Then it got smaller again. Same genes. Different gap.
blocks.screen_text: In 1900, the gap was only 2 years. By 1980, it was nearly 8. Then it got smaller again. Same genes. Different gap.

blocks.voice_text: That's a big clue. If it was only about being a man or a woman, the gap wouldn't swing like that. And part of the answer is simple. More men die before age sixty five. That pulls the average down.
blocks.screen_text: That's a big clue. If it was only about being a man or a woman, the gap wouldn't swing like that. And part of the answer is simple. More men die before age 65. That pulls the average down.

blocks.voice_text: So why do more men die young? Scientists still argue. Some point to habits. Some point to risks. Some point to biology. Nobody has the full answer.
blocks.screen_text: So why do more men die young? Scientists still argue. Some point to habits. Some point to risks. Some point to biology. Nobody has the full answer.

blocks.voice_text: Here's what we do know. Your body sends signals long before something goes wrong. Most of us never learn to read them. Comment the word glow, and I'll message you what your body is trying to tell you.

visual_style.mood: calm night, premium, curious. Never scary. No saturated red anywhere.

visual_style.silhouettes: flat dark-filled body shapes with a soft neon glow outline, women rose, men cyan, soft aura behind breathing on a 2.5 s sine; figures stay in y 520-1180

visual_style.data_visuals: vertical amber rulers with ticks and a glowing marker, count-up numbers (ease out 1.2 s), side-by-side comparisons, one big number per shot (140+ px)

typography.title: 96 px, white with one amber keyword, y 300-450, only the first 3 s
typography.karaoke: 76 px, spoken words white, current word amber, upcoming words dim gray, 3 words per line, 2 lines, baseline y 1330, centered
typography.rule: never show a title and subtitles with the same words at the same time

no red as a main color, nothing scary
a visual event every 2-3 s, every claim has a visual proof
only one text system at a time (title OR karaoke)
text inside safe zones, figures not hidden by subtitles
numbers on screen match the script, honesty chips where needed (e.g. small study, 2024 US data)
no health-result promises, prices, free, hashtags, music
